# dlaed5

> Solves the 2-by-2 secular equation.

<section class="intro">

Computes the I-th eigenvalue of a symmetric rank-one modification of a
2-by-2 diagonal matrix:

```text
diag( D ) + RHO * Z * transpose(Z)
```

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaed5 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlaed5';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaed5( i, D, strideD, Z, strideZ, DELTA, strideDELTA, rho, dlam ) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `i` | `integer` | Index of the eigenvalue to compute (1 or 2) |
| `D` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | Input array of length 2 containing the original eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `D` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | Input array of length 2 containing the updating vector components |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `Z` |
| `DELTA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | **out** · Output array of length 2 for eigenvector construction info |
| ↳ `strideDELTA` | `integer` | Stride length for `DELTA` |
| `rho` | `number` | Scalar in the symmetric updating formula |
| `dlam` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output array of length 1; `dlam[0]` receives the computed eigenvalue |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `i`: The index of the eigenvalue to be computed. $I = 1$ or $I = 2$.
- `D`: The original eigenvalues. We assume $D(1) < D(2)$.
- `Z`: The components of the updating vector.
- `DELTA`: The vector `DELTA` contains the information necessary to construct the eigenvectors.
- `rho`: The scalar in the symmetric updating formula.
- `dlam`: The computed lambda\_I, the I-th updated eigenvalue.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaed5.strided(
    i,
    D, strideD, offsetD,
    Z, strideZ, offsetZ,
    DELTA, strideDELTA, offsetDELTA,
    rho,
    dlam
) → Float64Array
```

Solves the 2-by-2 secular equation.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `i` | `integer` | Index of the eigenvalue to compute (1 or 2) |
| `D` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | Input array of length 2 containing the original eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `D` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `D` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 2</sub> | Input array of length 2 containing the updating vector components |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `Z` |

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlaed5()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAED5`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlaed5.f).

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlaed5 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlaed5';

// Original eigenvalues (D[0] < D[1]) and unit-norm updating vector:
const D = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 3.0 ] );
const Z = new Float64Array( [ 0.6, 0.8 ] );
const DELTA = new Float64Array( 2 );
const dlam = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rho = 0.5;

// Using the standard interface (first updated eigenvalue):
dlaed5( 1, D, 1, Z, 1, DELTA, 1, rho, dlam );
console.log( 'lambda1 = %d', dlam[ 0 ] );
console.log( DELTA );

// Using the strided interface (second updated eigenvalue):
dlaed5.strided( 2, D, 1, 0, Z, 1, 0, DELTA, 1, 0, rho, dlam );
console.log( 'lambda2 = %d', dlam[ 0 ] );
console.log( DELTA );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAED5`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

This subroutine computes the I-th eigenvalue of a symmetric rank-one modification of a 2-by-2 diagonal matrix

$\operatorname{diag}( D ) + \mathrm{RHO} \, Z$ \* transpose(Z) .

The diagonal elements in the array D are assumed to satisfy

$$
D(i) < D(j) \quad\text{for}\quad i < j
$$

We also assume $\mathrm{RHO} > 0$ and that the Euclidean norm of the vector Z is one.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
